column5: Flippant as usual, I see.\nListen — you need to learn more about that blade.\nYour life is on the line, so you need to start caring.
column6: 我看你还是老样子，油嘴滑舌的。\n听着——你需要多了解那把剑。\n你的命都搭在上面了，所以你得开始上心了。

column5: Without saying another word, he walks to the back alley.{w}\nI follow after him, ready to learn more about The Blade of Exodus.{w}\nWhen we arrive, I start to ask him questions. Mainly about its origin.
column6: 他一言不发地走向后巷。{w}\n我跟在他身后，准备好更多地了解流亡之刃。{w}\n抵达之后，我开始向他提问，主要是关于它的来历。

column5: I couldn't tell you. It's a mystery, even to me.\nPerhaps they stole it from The Monarchy before they took over.\nI've heard that they had visions, too. Much like the blade can supply.
column6: 我说不上来。这对我来说也是个谜。\n也许他们是在夺权之前从王室手里偷来的。\n我听说他们也能看到幻象，就像那把剑能提供的那样。

column5: If that's not the truth, then perhaps they made it themselves.\nBut I'm starting to think they either stole it, or stumbled upon it.\nStealing isn't above them, as we've all been made aware of.
column6: 如果事实并非如此，那也许就是他们自己造的。\n但我开始觉得，他们要么是偷来的，要么是偶然发现的。\n偷窃这种事他们干得出来，我们都已经领教过了。

column5: He shakes his head, as if he's upset that he can't sate my curiosity.{w}\nBut that's fine — perhaps it's something we'd find out when we went to Balteus.
column6: 他摇了摇头，似乎因为无法满足我的好奇心而有些懊恼。{w}\n不过没关系——也许等我们去巴尔泰乌斯的时候就能弄清楚了。

column5: This is probably the first trick I should teach you.
column6: 这大概是我该教你的第一招。

column5: He holds out a close fist, and my blade soon appears in his hand.{w}\nI've seen that happen several times. Almost like he can summon it at any time.
column6: 他握紧拳头伸出来，我的剑随即出现在他手中。{w}\n我见过好几次了，几乎像是他随时都能把它召唤过来。

column5: You have to be near the blade for it to work, but it's useful.\nDisarming your enemy is a viable tactic in battle, so be ready.\nThey will try to take the blade away from you, because of its power.
column6: 你得靠近那把剑才能做到，但这招很有用。\n缴械敌人是战斗中可行的战术，所以做好准备。\n他们会想从你手里夺走那把剑，因为它蕴含的力量。

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点点头。

column5: Go ahead. Hold out your hand and reach for the blade.\nNot with your body, but with your mind. See if it works.
column6: 来吧。伸出手，去够那把剑。\n不是用身体，而是用你的意念。看看能不能奏效。

column5: I close my eyes, and hold out my hand.{w}\nSovy immediately chastises me with the blunt side of the blade.{w}\nHitting it against my hand, I wince slightly and shake away the pain.
column6: 我闭上眼，伸出手。{w}\n索维立刻用剑的钝面教训了我。{w}\n剑身拍在我手上，我微微一缩，甩掉疼痛。

column5: No. Never close your eyes in battle.\nDid you not learn anything about combat in Valinorth...?\nIf you did that in a real battle, you'd be dead in mere seconds.
column6: 不行。战斗中绝不能闭眼。\n你在瓦利诺斯就没学到任何关于战斗的东西吗……？\n要是在真正的战斗中这么做，你几秒钟就没命了。

column5: I shrug.
column6: 我耸耸肩。

column5: Now do it again. And look me in the eye.\nI have no use for you if you can't follow directions.
column6: 再来一次。看着我的眼睛。\n要是你连指示都照做不了，你对我来说就没用。

column5: Doing as instructed, I look him in the eye.{w}\nI focus as hard as I can, and try to summon the blade.{w}\nBut after a few moments, nothing happens. Nothing at all.
column6: 我照着他的话做，直视他的眼睛。{w}\n我尽全力集中精神，试着召唤那把剑。{w}\n可过了片刻，什么也没发生。一点动静都没有。

column5: Try harder. Like your life depends on it.\nBecause when you need to do this — it will.
column6: 再用力些。就当你的命系于其上。\n因为当你真需要这么做的时候——确实如此。

column5: I scoff softly, but try not to break the gaze.{w}\nHe squints, as if he's judging my movements.{w}\nBut after even more time — nothing happens.
column6: 我轻哼一声，但尽量不移开视线。{w}\n他眯起眼，像是在审视我的动作。{w}\n可又过了更久——依然什么也没发生。

column5: I guess you need a little incentive.
column6: 看来你需要一点刺激。

column5: Without any warning, he reaches behind himself.{w}\nPulling a dagger from the leather straps on his back, he attacks me.{w}\nI take a defensive stance, and before he can harm me, I have possession of the blade.
column6: 毫无预警地，他伸手探向身后。{w}\n从背后的皮带里抽出一把匕首，向我攻来。{w}\n我摆出防御姿态，在他伤到我之前，剑已落入我手中。

column5: It appears in my hand, at the perfect angle and position to deflect Sovy's assault.{w}\nHis dagger is in deadlock with my blade, and he pushes me back against the alley wall.
column6: 它以完美的角度和位置出现在我手中，正好挡下索维的攻击。{w}\n他的匕首与我的剑僵持不下，他把我逼退到巷子的墙上。

column5: So it's your fear that powers you...
column6: 所以驱动你的是恐惧……

column5: After a few moments, he backs off, and puts away the dagger.
column6: 片刻之后，他退开，收起匕首。

column5: I was the same, until I mastered my fears.\nThen the blade responded to my willpower. My resolve.\nIt can learn and grow, just as much as you can, [firstname].
column6: 我也是这样，直到我驾驭了自己的恐惧。\n之后那把剑便回应我的意志，我的决心。\n它能学习和成长，就像你一样，[firstname]。

column5: If you learn to remain calm in the face of battle — you'll do fine.\nWithout fear to rely on, the blade will find something else.\nWhat that is, however, is different from person to person.
column6: 如果你学会在战斗面前保持冷静——你会做得很好。\n一旦没了恐惧可以依赖，剑会寻找别的东西。\n但那究竟是什么，因人而异。

column5: I'm eager to see what kind of person you become.\nFor now, let's continue on our way. No more wasting time.\nWhen we have another moment together, I can teach you more.
column6: 我迫不及待想看看你会成为什么样的人。\n眼下，我们继续赶路吧。别再浪费时间了。\n等我们再有机会独处，我可以多教你一些。

column5: He smiles and leaves the alleyway. I remain there by myself.{w}\nIt was hard {i}not{/i} to be scared, given my situation, and the upcoming battle.{w}\nBut if mastering those emotions made me a better wielder, then I had to try.
column6: 他笑了笑，离开了巷子。我独自留在那里。{w}\n考虑到我的处境和即将到来的战斗，要做到{i}不{/i}害怕很难。{w}\n但如果驾驭这些情绪能让我成为更好的持剑者，那我必须一试。

column5: I leave the alleyway, and replay the recent events in my mind.{w}\nMy eye trails over to the drawing utensils that Sovy pointed out earlier.{w}\nI wonder for a moment if I could get him a gift. A thank you for the lessons.
column6: 我离开巷子，在脑海里回放刚才发生的事。{w}\n我的目光落到索维先前指给我看的那些画具上。{w}\n我一时想着，能不能给他买件礼物，感谢他的教导。

column5: It seems harmless, so I stop and buy them on my way out of the town square.{w}\nI'd have to find the right chance to give them to him. It might take a while.{w}\nBut after that was said and done, it was time to get on my way.
column6: 看上去无伤大雅，于是我在离开城镇广场的路上停下来买下了它们。{w}\n我得找个合适的时机送给他，也许要等上一阵子。{w}\n但等这件事了结，我该继续上路了。

column5: It probably wasn't a good idea, so I forget it and move on.{w}\nPerhaps another time — as right now I was very busy.{w}\nI leave the town square, ready to continue on my way.
column6: 这大概不是什么好主意，于是我把这念头抛在脑后，继续往前走。{w}\n也许下次吧——毕竟我现在很忙。{w}\n我离开城镇广场，准备好继续赶路。

column5: As soon as we enter the Tavern, the smell of ale assaults our noses.{w}\nThis wasn't anything like Peregrino. This was on an entirely different level.{w} \nBottles of foreign alcohol line the shelves, I'd have no idea where to start looking.
column6: 我们一踏进酒馆，麦酒的气味便扑面而来。{w}\n这跟佩雷格里诺完全不一样。这完全是另一个档次。{w}\n架子上摆满了外国酒，我根本不知道该从哪里看起。

column5: Good call, [firstname].\nNo trip to Mazeo is complete without coming here.\nIf it's time to relax for a bit, I'll just take a seat at the bar.
column6: 好主意，[firstname]。\n不来这儿，马泽奥之行就不算完整。\n要是该放松一会儿，我就直接坐吧台边了。

column5: Good call, [firstname].\nNo trip to Mazeo is complete without coming here.\nIf it's time to relax for a bit, I'll just take a seat at the bar.
column6: 好主意，[firstname]。\n不来这儿，马泽奥之行就不算完整。\n要是该放松一会儿，我就直接坐吧台边了。

column5: He gives me a sly smirk, and immediately takes a seat.{w}\nA bartender, who I can only describe as overwhelmed, takes his order.{w}\nPro takes a few steps forward, and afterwards, takes a deep breath.
column6: 他冲我狡黠一笑，随即坐了下来。{w}\n一个我只能用忙得焦头烂额来形容的酒保来记下他的点单。{w}\n普洛往前走了几步，随后深吸一口气。

column5: You just can't beat that smell!\nIf you need me, I'll just be checking my mail.\nI've been in Valinorth for a while. I'd hate to miss anything.
column6: 这味道真是无可匹敌！\n要是你找我，我就在那边查看信件。\n我在瓦利诺斯待了好一阵子，可不想错过什么消息。

column5: Trotting off to the corner, he starts to inspect his mailbox.{w}\nShelves with letters and numbers line the back corner of The Tavern.{w}\nHe must pay to have an anonymous address, or something like that.
column6: 他快步走到角落，开始翻看自己的信箱。{w}\n酒馆后角排着一列标有字母和数字的架子。{w}\n他一定是花钱弄了个匿名地址，或者类似的什么。

column5: Taverns don't really do anything for me, [firstname].\nI don't mean any offense by this — but I'll be waiting outside.\nThat's not to rush your relaxation, or anything. You deserve it.
column6: 酒馆对我没什么吸引力，[firstname]。\n我无意冒犯——但我会在外面等着。\n不是要催你放松，绝对不是。你当之无愧。

column5: Taverns don't really do anything for me, [firstname].\nI don't mean any offense by this — but I'll be waiting outside.\nThat's not to rush your relaxation, or anything. You deserve it.
column6: 酒馆对我没什么吸引力，[firstname]。\n我无意冒犯——但我会在外面等着。\n不是要催你放松，绝对不是。你当之无愧。

column5: With a smile, he slowly backs out of the Tavern.{w}\nI guess this would be a good chance to talk with Pro and Ulric.{w}\nWe haven't really had enough time to get to know each other yet.
column6: 他微微一笑，慢慢退出了酒馆。{w}\n我想这是个跟普洛和乌尔里克聊聊的好机会。{w}\n我们一直没有足够的时间彼此了解。

column5: Valessa and Fortaime take a seat and start talking amongst themselves.{w}\nI guess it wouldn't be the end of the world if we wasted a {i}little{/i} bit of time here.{w}\nUlric is chugging a large cup of ale, and Pro is carefully reading over some letters.
column6: 瓦莱莎和福泰姆找了个位置坐下，彼此攀谈起来。{w}\n我想，在这儿浪费{i}一点点{/i}时间也没什么大不了的。{w}\n乌尔里克正大口灌着一大杯麦酒，普洛则在仔细翻阅几封信。

column5: It's a book on Alarinthia's Civil Conflict.
column6: 这是一本关于阿拉林西亚内乱的书。

column5: I examine the shelves, looking for anything of note.{w}\nI don't find much, except for a piece on some current news.{w}\nIt couldn't hurt to get a better perspective on Alestia's current state.
column6: 我打量书架，寻找值得注意的东西。{w}\n没找到多少，只看到一篇关于时事的报道。{w}\n多了解一下阿莱斯蒂亚的现状也无妨。

column5: Resting my back against the shelf, I start to read it.{w}\nIt seems to be about Alarinthia. Ulric's homeland.{w}\nApparently, things aren't going very well over there.
column6: 我背靠书架，开始读起来。{w}\n似乎是关于阿拉林西亚，乌尔里克的故乡。{w}\n显然，那边的局势不太妙。

column5: I wonder who this \"Vivienne\" is.{w}\nUlric would definitely side with someone like her.{w}\nHe thinks that Alarinthia should be more like the mainland.
column6: 我想知道这个“薇薇安”是谁。{w}\n乌尔里克肯定会站在她这样的人一边。{w}\n他认为阿拉林西亚应该更像大陆那边。

column5: So, you ever drink this stuff before?
column6: 那么，你以前喝过这种酒吗？

column5: He motions up to the bar, gesturing broadly at everything.{w}\nI've never seen bottles of alcohol like that, so I'm totally clueless.{w}\nWe're in a completely different region of Alestia. It's all new to me.
column6: 他朝吧台抬了抬下巴，挥手笼统地比划着一切。{w}\n我从没见过那样的酒瓶，所以完全摸不着头脑。{w}\n我们身处阿莱斯蒂亚截然不同的地区。这一切对我来说都是陌生的。

column5: You'll have to join me.\nI can pick out the good stuff.\nWithout me, you'd just be wasting time.
column6: 你得陪我喝一杯。\n好酒我能挑得出来。\n没我在，你只会白白浪费时间。

column5: Half the stuff on display isn't even that good.\nTo be honest, they keep a lot of the good stuff down there.
column6: 摆出来的有一半根本没那么好。\n说实话，好东西他们大多藏在下面。

column5: He points underneath the bar. I guess that made sense.
column6: 他指了指吧台下面。我想这倒也说得通。

column5: Cheers, by the way.
column6: 顺便，干杯。

column5: He holds up his glass, before taking a huge swig of ale.
column6: 他举起杯子，然后闷了一大口麦酒。

column5: It just doesn't compare to what they had at Peregrino.\nAnyway, I'll let you take care of your business. I'm right here.
column6: 这根本比不上佩雷格里诺的酒。\n总之，你去忙你的事吧。我就在这儿。

column5: So, are you having a drink?
column6: 那么，你要来一杯吗？

column5: No, I'm good.\nThere's too much to focus on.
column6: 不，我不用。\n要操心的事太多了。

column5: You gotta do it sometime, you know.
column6: 你知道，你总得喝一回的。

column5: Maybe after all this blows over.
column6: 也许等这一切平息之后吧。

column5: That could take forever!\nYou should take some time to unwind.
column6: 那可能得等到天荒地老！\n你该抽点时间放松一下。

column5: Are {i}you{/i} getting something...?
column6: {i}你{/i}要点什么吗……？

column5: Yeah, I'm still deciding, though.\nI don't know any of this stuff on the menu.\nIt's like we're in a completely different world.
column6: 是啊，不过我还在犹豫。\n菜单上的东西我一个都不认识。\n就像我们身处一个完全不同的世界。

column5: Didn't Ulric have to buy you that apple earlier?\nWhere are you getting the money to order this stuff?
column6: 刚才那个苹果不是乌尔里克帮你买的吗？\n你哪来的钱点这些东西？

column5: Oh... Good question.\nI'm used to the way things are in Valinorth.\nAlmost everything is provided to us, because of our roles.
column6: 哦……问得好。\n我习惯了瓦利诺斯的处事方式。\n因为我们的身份，几乎所有东西都是配给我们的。

column5: Yeah, fair enough.\nMaybe you should go sweet-talk Ulric.\nIf it's on him, maybe I'll consider trying something.
column6: 是啊，有道理。\n也许你该去哄哄乌尔里克。\n要是他请客，也许我会考虑尝一尝。

column5: Sounds good.\nI think he likes me, so this'll be easy.\nWait here — we'll try the fanciest thing on the menu.
column6: 听起来不错。\n我觉得他挺喜欢我，所以这很容易。\n在这儿等着——我们要尝尝菜单上最贵的东西。

column5: Pro rests his back against the mailboxes, sifting through letters.{w}\nHe must be pretty popular, as his hands were full of paper.{w}\nI can't even imagine if I got that many letters in Valinorth.
column6: 普洛背靠着信箱，翻拣着信件。{w}\n他一定很受欢迎，手里满是纸张。{w}\n我简直无法想象要是在瓦利诺斯收到这么多信会是什么样。

column5: Oh — hey there!
column6: 哦——你好啊！

column5: He looks up at me, startled, and turns to face the mailboxes.{w}\nAs if in a rush, he starts putting various letters in various boxes.{w}\nWait — all of those letters weren't actually his? Uh-oh.
column6: 他吓了一跳，抬头看我，随即转身面对信箱。{w}\n他像是赶时间似的，开始把各种信件塞进不同的信箱。{w}\n等等——那些信其实都不是他的？糟了。

column5: Well, you caught me.\nJust don't tell anybody else, alright?\nThis is one of the best ways to get \"information\".
column6: 好吧，被你逮到了。\n只要别告诉别人，行吗？\n这是获取“情报”最好的办法之一。

column5: You'd think so, but here we are.\nI've been doing it for years with no complaints.\nI just make sure the box owners aren't nearby.
column6: 你大概会这么想，可事实就是如此。\n我干这行好几年了，从没人抱怨。\n我只要确保信箱主人不在附近就行。

column5: They all have schedules and jobs, you know.\nI have this thing down to a science. I'll never get caught.\nIt's just a steady supply of juicy secret after juicy secret.
column6: 你知道，他们都各有作息和工作。\n我把这事做得像门科学，绝不会被抓到。\n源源不断的，就是一条又一条劲爆的秘密。

column5: Oh? An accomplice...?\nI've never actually thought about that.\nI guess it {i}could{/i} make things a little easier.
column6: 哦？一个同伙……？\n我还真没想过这个。\n我想这{i}确实{/i}能让事情稍微轻松些。

column5: Stand guard for me, alright?\nLet me know if anybody approaches.\nIf I get caught, I can play it off as a misunderstanding.
column6: 替我望风，好吗？\n有人靠近就告诉我。\n要是我被抓到，我可以把它说成是场误会。

column5: \"Oh, don't worry! Just a little mixup!\"\nTrust me, it works pretty much every time I'm caught.\nIt's so easy to win people over. Just admit you did something wrong.
column6: “哦，别担心！只是弄错了而已！”\n相信我，每次被抓到这招几乎都管用。\n赢得别人的好感太容易了。只要承认自己做错了事。

column5: They'll immediately switch their stance to defend you.\n\"Oh, don't worry about it! It's not a big deal!\"\nPeople work in such weird ways.
column6: 他们会立刻转变立场来替你说话。\n“哦，别放在心上！又不是什么大事！”\n人的心思就是这么奇怪。

column5: Oh? Are you trying to blackmail me?\nHonestly, I didn't think you were the type.\nI'm immediately more interested in you.
column6: 哦？你想勒索我？\n说实话，我没看出你是这种人。\n我立刻对你更感兴趣了。

column5: But — to be honest — that won't work on me.\nI can play my way out of pretty much any situation.\nSo do your worst, and I promise I'll adapt.
column6: 不过——说实话——那对我没用。\n几乎任何局面我都能靠手段脱身。\n所以尽管放马过来，我保证我能随机应变。

column5: Good, that's exactly what I wanted to hear.\nNow if you'll excuse me, I need to get back to business.\nI don't have much longer until these box owners stop by.
column6: 很好，这正是我想听到的。\n那么失陪了，我得回去忙正事。\n离这些信箱主人过来已经没多久了。

column5: He turns back to the mailboxes, and raids them once again.{w}\nI guess he assumed it was okay, since I was one of his comrades.{w}\nA big smile appears on his face as he \"borrows\" private information.
column6: 他转回信箱，再次大肆搜刮。{w}\n我想他以为没关系，因为我是他的同伴之一。{w}\n当他“借阅”私人信息时，脸上浮现出大大的笑容。

column5: It's amazing what some of these people get up to.\nThe most innocent people could be involved in awful things.\nSee — I can beat blackmail — but these people can't.
column6: 这些人干出的事真是令人惊叹。\n最看上去无辜的人也可能牵扯进可怕的事情里。\n你看——我能扛住勒索——但这些人不能。

column5: It's a good way to line The Rebellion's coffers.\nSo later today, I'm gonna pay this guy a visit.
column6: 这是充实反抗军金库的好办法。\n所以今天晚些时候，我要去拜访这家伙。

column5: He taps one of the papers in his hands.
column6: 他轻敲手中一张纸。

column5: It would seem a \"reputable\" business owner is up to no good.\nI think he'd lose some business if people found out he worked with pirates.\nIf I got him to pay me off, I could feed The Rebellion for months, [firstname]!
column6: 看来一位“声名良好”的商人正在干着见不得人的勾当。\n我想，要是人们发现他跟海盗有往来，他的生意会损失一些。\n要是我能让他掏钱封口，就能养活反抗军好几个月，[firstname]！

column5: It would seem a \"reputable\" business owner is up to no good.\nI think he'd lose some business if people found out he worked with pirates.\nIf I got him to pay me off, I could feed The Rebellion for months, [firstname]!
column6: 看来一位“声名良好”的商人正在干着见不得人的勾当。\n我想，要是人们发现他跟海盗有往来，他的生意会损失一些。\n要是我能让他掏钱封口，就能养活反抗军好几个月，[firstname]！

column5: He looks at me, as if waiting for my approval.
column6: 他看着我，像是在等我的首肯。

column5: Is everything okay...?\nI'm not scaring you away, am I?\nThis kinda stuff isn't for everybody.
column6: 你还好吗……？\n我没把你吓跑吧？\n这种事不是人人都受得了的。

column5: Now you're talking! This'll be my biggest score in months.\nI'll get it done tonight, and then celebrate in my room back at HQ.\nFeel free to pay me a visit, I'd be down for some quality time together.
column6: 这才对嘛！这会是我几个月来最大的一票。\n我今晚就把它办妥，然后回总部房间里庆祝。\n欢迎你来找我，我很乐意一起共度些美好时光。

column5: Damek turns a blind eye to it, you know.\nIt's better to keep our soldiers strong and fed.\nWithout my \"excursions\", everybody would starve.
column6: 你知道，达梅克对此睁一只眼闭一只眼。\n让我们的士兵吃饱、强壮总归是好事。\n没有我的“外快”，大家都会挨饿。

column5: You'll have to get used to it, one way or another.\nI'm doing this tonight — and then I'll celebrate in my room back at HQ.\nFeel free to pay me a visit if you change your mind. We can hang out.
column6: 不管怎样，你都得习惯它。\n我今晚就动手——然后回总部房间里庆祝。\n要是你改变主意，欢迎来找我。我们可以一起玩玩。

column5: I mean, you still want to be friends — right?\nI hope all of this danger doesn't scare you away.\nI'm not like this all the time. Trust me, [firstname].
column6: 我是说，你还是想做朋友吧——对吧？\n希望这些危险不会把你吓跑。\n我不是一直都这样的。相信我，[firstname]。

column5: I mean, you still want to be friends — right?\nI hope all of this danger doesn't scare you away.\nI'm not like this all the time. Trust me, [firstname].
column6: 我是说，你还是想做朋友吧——对吧？\n希望这些危险不会把你吓跑。\n我不是一直都这样的。相信我，[firstname]。

column5: Wow, that's pretty forward.\nDoes this \"danger stuff\" turn you on, or something?\nYou know what? Don't answer that. At least, not here.
column6: 哇，你可真直接。\n这种“危险勾当”让你兴奋还是怎么的？\n算了，别回答。至少别在这儿回答。

column5: Look, I have no idea what you're after.\nBut to be honest, I don't know what I'm after, either.\nIf you want to pay me a visit later, we'll see what happens.
column6: 听着，我不知道你图什么。\n但说实话，我自己也不知道我图什么。\n要是你之后想来拜访我，我们就走着瞧吧。

column5: My room back at HQ is pretty big and luxurious.\nWe can crack open a bottle of wine to celebrate my big score.\nI'm not going to promise any more than that, alright?
column6: 我在总部的房间又大又奢华。\n我们可以开一瓶酒庆祝我这次大捞一笔。\n我不会承诺更多，行吗？

column5: Good, I'm glad.\nYou caught me, so I had to come clean.\nOtherwise, I would've kept this stuff secret.
column6: 很好，我很高兴。\n你逮到我了，所以我只好坦白。\n不然的话，我会把这事一直瞒着。

column5: Not many people know what I \"actually\" do.\nBut, if you pay attention, it's not too much of a stretch.\nIt's just something I picked up from years on the streets.
column6: 没多少人知道我“真正”在做什么。\n不过，只要你留心，其实也不算太难猜到。\n这只是我在街头混了多年学来的东西。

column5: Maybe I'll tell you a bit more back at HQ.\nI'll use this big score to buy a bottle of wine.\nWe can crack it open and get to know each other.
column6: 也许回总部后我会多告诉你一些。\n我会用这次大捞一笔的钱买瓶酒。\n我们可以开瓶畅饮，彼此认识认识。

column5: Hmm. Fair enough.\nNot everybody is built for this kind of stuff.\nBut to be honest, I {i}do{/i} want to learn more about you.
column6: 嗯。有道理。\n不是人人都适合这种事。\n但说实话，我{i}确实{/i}想多了解你一些。

column5: I can win you over, yet. Especially if you have wiggle room.\nTell you what — I'll use this big score to pick up a bottle of wine.\nWe can crack it open back at HQ and get to know each other better.
column6: 我还是能说服你的。尤其要是你还有回旋的余地。\n这样吧——我会用这次大捞一笔的钱买瓶酒。\n回总部后我们可以开瓶畅饮，更好地了解彼此。

column5: He carefully places the letters back in their respective mailboxes.{w}\nClapping his hands together, as if to brush off dust, he looks right at me.{w}\nSquinting his eyes, it's almost like he's trying to \"judge\" or \"gauge\" me.
column6: 他小心地把信件放回各自的信箱。{w}\n他双掌相击，像是要掸去灰尘，然后直视着我。{w}\n他眯起眼睛，几乎像是在“评判”或“估量”我。

column5: I gotta admit, you're a bit different than I expected.\nThat's surprising, since I'm usually a good judge of character.\nYou'd make an interesting subject to write about, you know.
column6: 我得承认，你和我预想的不太一样。\n这很让人意外，毕竟我通常看人挺准的。\n你知道吗，你会是个很有意思的写作对象。

column5: I shrug, unsure of how to respond to such a thing.
column6: 我耸耸肩，不知该如何回应这种话。

column5: Now I'm getting ahead of myself. I apologize.\nLet's just stick to the plan. Bottle of wine. Rebel HQ.\nI have a new target, so I should probably get going.
column6: 我这下又说太远了，抱歉。\n我们还是按计划来吧。一瓶酒。反抗军总部。\n我有新目标了，大概该走了。

column5: He smiles at me and rests a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 他冲我一笑，一只手搭在我肩上。

column5: There's not many people I can talk to about this kinda stuff.\nIf I have to be honest, I'd say I'm kinda glad that you caught me.\nNext time we talk it'll be your turn to spill some secrets, alright?
column6: 能聊这种事的人，我没几个。\n要我说实话，我还挺高兴被你逮到的。\n下次聊天就该轮到你吐露些秘密了，行吗？

column5: With a sly smirk, he slowly walks away from the mailbox.{w}\nI guess now I know a little bit more about Pro's true nature.{w}\nBut in a time of war, I guess you had to resort to stuff like that.
column6: 他狡黠一笑，慢慢从信箱旁走开。{w}\n我想我现在多了解了一点普洛的真面目。{w}\n但在战时，人大概不得不诉诸这种手段。

column5: Damek must only allow it out of necessity.{w}\nI'm sure Pro would stop this behavior once the war was over.{w}\nSo rather than condemn him, I choose to take him up on his offer.
column6: 达梅克一定只是出于无奈才纵容它。{w}\n我相信战争结束后普洛就会停止这种行为。{w}\n所以与其谴责他，我选择接受他的邀请。

column5: Learning more about him over a drink could prove to be entertaining.{w}\nAnd at the end of the day, it wouldn't hurt to make another friend.{w}\nI turn back to the tavern, ready to move on to the next step.
column6: 边喝边多了解他，想必挺有意思。{w}\n而且说到底，多交个朋友也没什么坏处。{w}\n我转身回到酒馆，准备进入下一步。

column5: I sit down beside Ulric and look over at him.{w}\nA couple empty glasses strewn about signal that he's already had a few.{w}\nHowever, he doesn't seem to show it. Not at all. He's calm and collected.
column6: 我在乌尔里克身旁坐下，望向他。{w}\n散落的几个空杯说明他已经喝了几杯。{w}\n可他一点也看不出来。完全没有。他镇定自若。

column5: Hey, [firstname]. Come to join me?\nI can recommend a few drinks if you'd like.\nDo you want something strong, or should we start weak?
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。来陪我喝一杯吗？\n要是你愿意，我可以推荐几款酒。\n你想来点烈的，还是先从不烈的开始？

column5: Hey, [firstname]. Come to join me?\nI can recommend a few drinks if you'd like.\nDo you want something strong, or should we start weak?
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。来陪我喝一杯吗？\n要是你愿意，我可以推荐几款酒。\n你想来点烈的，还是先从不烈的开始？

column5: Perfect choice.\nHey Barkeep, more of the same.
column6: 完美的选择。\n嘿，酒保，再来一样的。

column5: He motions to the bartender, and a few moments later, I'm given a glass.{w}\nUlric watches me with a smirk as I take a large swig, and swallow it down.{w}\nIt's strong, almost enough to make me cough — but I maintain my cool.
column6: 他朝酒保示意，片刻之后，我面前多了一杯酒。{w}\n我大口喝下、咽下去时，乌尔里克带着坏笑看着我。{w}\n这酒很烈，几乎让我咳出来——但我保持着镇定。

column5: I thought that'd be a bit much, honestly.\nGood to know you can handle it like that.\nIt's strong, but not quite on my level.
column6: 老实说，我以为这对你来说会太烈。\n很高兴知道你扛得住。\n它很烈，但还不到我那个水平。

column5: I guess we'll have to work our way up.\nDon't worry, you'll get to my level in no time.
column6: 看来我们得一步步往上爬了。\n别担心，你很快就会达到我的水平。

column5: He motions to the bartender, and a few moments later, I'm given a glass.{w}\nUlric watches me with a smirk as I take a large swig, and swallow it down.{w}\nIt tastes like nothing. Practically water. Weak was actually an understatement.
column6: 他朝酒保示意，片刻之后，我面前多了一杯酒。{w}\n我大口喝下、咽下去时，乌尔里克带着坏笑看着我。{w}\n这酒尝起来什么味道都没有，简直是水。说它不烈都算是高估了。

column5: Wish you went for the stronger one?\nTrust me, I started out the same way.\nSometimes, you just need to dive in.
column6: 后悔没选更烈的那个吧？\n相信我，我一开始也是这样。\n有时候，你就得一头扎进去。

column5: Want another one...?\nWhat're you in the mood for?
column6: 再来一杯……？\n你想喝什么？

column5: Now you're talking.\nHere, I promise you won't regret this.
column6: 这才对嘛。\n来，我保证你不会后悔。

column5: Once again, he motions to the bartender, and I'm given a drink.{w}\nI can tell that this one is stronger. It's exactly the same as Ulric's.{w}\nAs time passes, I notice him start to exhibit signs of inebriation.
column6: 他再次朝酒保示意，我又得到一杯酒。{w}\n我看得出这杯更烈。和乌尔里克那杯一模一样。{w}\n随着时间流逝，我注意到他开始显出醉意。

column5: I grip the glass, and take a large swig. It burns.{w}\nMy eyes shoot wide open, and I try not to spit it out.{w}\nIt's a brief battle, but I eventually stomach it all.
column6: 我握紧杯子，大口喝下。喉咙火辣辣的。{w}\n我双眼猛地睁大，努力不把它喷出来。{w}\n一番短暂的挣扎，我最终还是咽了下去。

column5: Wow, you're good.\nMost people can't handle this stuff.\nMazeo is known for its strong liquor.
column6: 哇，你真行。\n大多数人受不了这玩意儿。\n马泽奥以烈酒闻名。

column5: Alright, one step at a time.\nHold on, I'll get you something special.
column6: 好吧，一步一步来。\n等等，我给你弄点特别的。

column5: Once again, he motions to the bartender, and I'm given a drink.{w}\nThis one is tinted red, like a fruit. Perhaps it wouldn't be too bad.{w}\nAs time passes, I notice him start to exhibit signs of inebriation.
column6: 他再次朝酒保示意，我又得到一杯酒。{w}\n这杯泛着红色，像是果酒。也许不至于太糟。{w}\n随着时间流逝，我注意到他开始显出醉意。

column5: I grip the glass, and take a large swig. It's very fruity.{w}\nThere's a bit of a burn, but it's nothing too bad. I drink it all.{w}\nSlamming the glass down on the table, I declare my victory.
column6: 我握紧杯子，大口喝下。果味很浓。{w}\n有点辣，但不算太糟。我一饮而尽。{w}\n我把杯子砰地砸在桌上，宣告我的胜利。

column5: Okay, that one was easy.\nBut like I said, one step at a time.\nThe night is just getting started.
column6: 好吧，那杯不算什么。\n但就像我说的，一步一步来。\n夜晚才刚开始。

column5: He crosses his arms, and stares at me with a blank look.{w}\nBut soon after, his facial expression becomes more stern.{w}\nIt's clear that the drinks are starting to hit him, and fast.
column6: 他抱起双臂，面无表情地盯着我。{w}\n但没过多久，他脸上的神情变得更严肃。{w}\n显然，酒劲开始上来了，而且来得很猛。

column5: I guess I'll stop messing with you for now.\nTruth is, I just wanted to see how much you could handle.\nIt's a good test. A nice judge of character; and you passed.
column6: 我想我暂时不逗你了。\n其实，我只是想看看你能喝多少。\n这是个不错的考验，能很好地看人品；而你通过了。

column5: He was testing me...?
column6: 他是在考验我……？

column5: You learn a lot about someone by how they hold their liquor.\nYou're strong. At least, you have a strong will. I respect that.\nThis is part of how they do things back in Alarinthia.
column6: 从一个人喝酒的样子能看出很多。\n你很强。至少，你意志坚强。我敬重这一点。\n在阿拉林西亚，这也是他们行事方式的一部分。

column5: I know I say I hate it, and I truly do. \nBut some of its culture sticks with me.\nYou left Valinorth, so it'll likely be the same.
column6: 我知道我说过我恨它，我确实恨。\n但它的某些文化还是留在了我身上。\n你离开了瓦利诺斯，大概也会一样。

column5: He waves to the bartender, who brings him another drink.{w}\nHonestly, I'm surprised he's still coherent. That's crazy.{w}\nSwigging it down, he lets out a sigh of complete content.
column6: 他向酒保招手，酒保又给他端来一杯。{w}\n说实话，他居然还条理清晰，我很惊讶。简直不可思议。{w}\n他一口气灌下，发出一声无比满足的叹息。

column5: Sorry for rambling on like that.\nIf there's anything I hate, it's a one-sided conversation.\nIs there anything you want to ask me? Right now, I'm an open book.
column6: 抱歉我那样絮絮叨叨。\n要说我讨厌什么，那就是单方面的谈话。\n有什么想问我的吗？现在我就是本摊开的书。

column5: There isn't one to talk about. But that's by choice.\nI prefer to keep things casual, without any strings.\nI have my reasons, but it's served me just fine.
column6: 没什么可谈的对象。但这是我自己的选择。\n我更喜欢随性而为，不被束缚。\n我有我的理由，而这样对我一直挺管用。

column5: He smiles at me, and takes another swig of his drink.
column6: 他冲我一笑，又喝了一大口。

column5: Don't worry, I've definitely noticed your interest.\nSo that's why I'm making things as clear as possible.\nKnowing that, do you {i}really{/i} want to continue down this path?
column6: 别担心，我当然注意到了你的兴趣。\n所以我才要把话尽量说清楚。\n知道这些之后，你{i}真的{/i}还想继续走下去吗？

column5: Good to know, because I share the same interest.\nWhen you live as long as I have, you pick up on these things.\nNo need to make a big deal out of this. It's just fun.
column6: 很高兴知道，因为我也有同样的兴趣。\n当你活得像我这么久，自然能察觉到这些。\n没必要把这事看得太重。不过是图个乐子。

column5: When we get back to our new HQ, Damek will give you a tour.\nMy doors are open. If you want to do this, I'll be there.\nJust don't tell anyone. You know how rumors spread.
column6: 等我们回到新总部，达梅克会带你四处看看。\n我的门随时敞开。要是你想这样，我会在。\n只是别告诉任何人。你知道流言传得多快。

column5: No worries. Everybody is different.\nThanks for being honest, though. \nSo, we'll just be drinking buddies?
column6: 没关系。人各有不同。\n不过谢谢你这么坦诚。\n那么，我们就只是酒友了？

column5: I'm fine with that.\nIt's been a long time since I've done this.\nDamek always had me running all over the place.
column6: 我没意见。\n我很久没这样了。\n达梅克总是让我到处奔波。

column5: Honestly, there's not much more to say.\nI'm a man between two worlds, and it's complicated.\nIt's hard to shake the habits of where we come from.
column6: 说实话，也没什么更多好说的了。\n我是个夹在两个世界之间的人，这很复杂。\n我们来自哪里的习惯，很难摆脱。

column5: I think so, yeah.\nWe'll have lots of work to do after we win this war.\nBut making the world a better place? That includes Valinorth.
column6: 我想是的。\n赢下这场战争后，我们会有很多事要做。\n但让世界变得更好？那也包括瓦利诺斯。

column5: Either way, I think I've had enough.\nI'm gonna buy a bottle to bring to my chambers.\nFeel free to join me if you want to share another drink.
column6: 不管怎样，我想我喝够了。\n我要买瓶酒带回我的房间。\n要是你想再喝一杯，欢迎来陪我。

column5: I nod and stand up, but all of the drinks hit me at once.{w}\nI stumble back, and Ulric catches me, wrapping his arms around me.
column6: 我点头起身，可所有的酒一下子全涌上来。{w}\n我踉跄后退，乌尔里克扶住我，双臂环住我。

column5: Hey now, watch your step.\nThe ground here could do some real damage.
column6: 嘿，当心脚下。\n这地方的地面可是能摔出真伤来的。

column5: Rather than letting go, he lets his hands wander around my body.{w}\nMy heartrate increases, and I feel his hot breaths strike my neck.
column6: 他没有松手，反而任双手在我身上游移。{w}\n我的心跳加快，感到他滚烫的呼吸打在我脖子上。

column5: Actually, I think I'll get a few bottles for my place.\nSomething tells me we'll be having more fun than I thought.
column6: 其实，我想给我的住处多买几瓶。\n我有种感觉，我们会比我想的更有乐子。

column5: A few moments later, before overstepping any boundaries, he lets me go.{w}\nBuying a few bottles of wine, he keeps his word before moving on to other things.{w}\nSocializing with the tavern patrons, it seemed like our moment was over.
column6: 片刻之后，在逾越任何界限之前，他放开了我。{w}\n他买了几瓶酒，信守了诺言，然后转而去做别的事。{w}\n他同酒馆里的客人寒暄起来，看来我们的时刻已经过去。

column5: I nod and stand up, but all of the drinks hit me at once.{w}\nI immediately stumble over, using the bar to brace myself.
column6: 我点头起身，可所有的酒一下子全涌上来。{w}\n我当即踉跄了一下，扶着吧台稳住自己。

column5: Hey now, watch your step.\nThe ground here could do some real damage.
column6: 嘿，当心脚下。\n这地方的地面可是能摔出真伤来的。

column5: I shake my head, and regain my clarity.{w}\nIt's a mystery to me how Ulric could handle this stuff.{w}\nIt would be a long time before I reached his level.
column6: 我摇摇头，恢复了清醒。{w}\n乌尔里克怎么能受得了这种酒，对我来说是个谜。{w}\n要赶上他的水平，我还早得很。

column5: True to his word, Ulric orders a bottle of alcohol, and walks away.{w}\nSocializing with the tavern patrons, it seemed like our moment was over.{w}\nI take a few deep breaths, and ensure my head is clear before moving.
column6: 乌尔里克说到做到，点了一瓶酒，转身走开。{w}\n他同酒馆里的客人寒暄起来，看来我们的时刻已经过去。{w}\n我深吸几口气，确认头脑清醒后才挪步。

column5: I guess we had to get things back on track.{w}\nAs enjoyable as that was, we had business to take care of.{w}\nHopefully we had more time like this to unwind in the future.
column6: 我想我们得把正事重新提上日程了。{w}\n尽管刚才很愉快，我们还有事要办。{w}\n希望将来能有更多像这样放松的时光。

column5: We follow after Damek, and embark on what seems like an endless journey.{w}\nHowever, after an hour or so of walking, we end up in a residential area.{w}\nThe buildings here are built beautifully. Very different from before.
column6: 我们跟在达梅克身后，踏上一段似乎没有尽头的旅程。{w}\n不过，走了大约一个小时后，我们来到一片住宅区。{w}\n这里的建筑造得很漂亮，和之前所见大不相同。

column5: Wow, this place looks incredible!\nThat town square was a little bit “off”.\nNot the best first impression, if you ask me.
column6: 哇，这地方看起来太棒了！\n那个城镇广场有点“不对劲”。\n要我说，可算不上最好的第一印象。

column5: It's a sign of wealth to live far away from the markets.\nOnly those who {i}work{/i}, live near the town square.\nOnce you've got it made — you move out here.
column6: 住得离集市远，是财富的象征。\n只有{i}干活{/i}的人才住在城镇广场附近。\n一旦你飞黄腾达——就搬到这边来。

column5: That is, of course, unless you're important to Mazeo.\nGryz gets to live here free of charge for his services.\nThat offer even extends to Lillith, his assistant.
column6: 当然，除非你对马泽奥很重要。\n格瑞兹因为他的功绩，得以免费住在这里。\n这份优待甚至惠及他的助手莉莉丝。

column5: You mean like our Elder back in Valinorth?
column6: 你是说像我们在瓦利诺斯的长老那样？

column5: Yeah, exactly. So make sure to be careful.\nIn this district, pretty much everyone is royalty.\nOr at least, they expect to be treated that way.
column6: 对，正是如此。所以务必小心。\n这个区里，几乎人人都算得上贵族。\n至少，他们希望被那样对待。

column5: Alright. Thanks for the advice, Damek.
column6: 好吧。谢谢你的提醒，达梅克。

column5: She moves to the back of the group, almost like she's worried.{w}\nWe continue to walk, but not for much longer. Damek stops in his tracks.
column6: 她走到队伍后面，几乎像是有些担忧。{w}\n我们继续走着，但没走多久，达梅克就停下了脚步。

column5: To your right — Gryz's office.\nSorry it took a while, but you know how it is.\nIt'll be an even longer trek back to our new HQ.
column6: 你的右手边——格瑞兹的办公室。\n抱歉花了这么久，但你也知道情况。\n回新总部的路还要更长呢。

column5: He laughs and motions to the nearby building.{w}\nIt stood out from the rest in both quality and size.
column6: 他笑着指向近旁的建筑。{w}\n无论品质还是规模，它都在其余建筑中脱颖而出。

column5: It's time for you to tell us what's going on.\nI hate being left in the dark like this. You know that.
column6: 该你告诉我们到底怎么回事了。\n我讨厌像这样被蒙在鼓里。你知道的。

column5: Of course, of course. You know I'm a man of my word.\nI just didn't like talking about this stuff in the Town Square.
column6: 当然，当然。你知道我说话算话。\n我只是不喜欢在城镇广场谈这些事。

column5: He cracks his knuckles, like he's preparing for something.{w}\nHe faces toward Valessa, Fortaime, and myself with a smile.{w}\nIt's almost like he assumes that Ulric and Pro are up to speed.
column6: 他掰了掰指关节，像是要准备什么。{w}\n他面带微笑，面向瓦莱莎、福泰姆和我。{w}\n几乎像是他认定乌尔里克和普洛已经了解情况了。

column5: Well, as you know, Mazeo is rampant with piracy.\nAll of that chaos needs some sort of order — right?\nTwo pirates have risen to the challenge. Alex and Nada.
column6: 嗯，如你所知，马泽奥海盗横行。\n那样的混乱总需要某种秩序——对吧？\n两名海盗挺身而出，担起了这个重任。亚历克斯和娜达。

column5: Unifying all of the pirates isn't an easy task, but they did it.\nThey have established trade routes and the largest fleet in the world.\nWe want to strike a deal with them and gain some ships. Easy, right?
column6: 统一所有海盗绝非易事，但他们做到了。\n他们建立了贸易航线，拥有世界上最大的舰队。\n我们想跟他们达成协议，弄到一些船。简单，对吧？

column5: When we attack Balteus, we won't be able to hold back.\nHaving enough ships to carry our massive army over is essential.\nAnd if we can get the pirates to fight with us? Even better.
column6: 我们进攻巴尔泰乌斯时，绝不能留手。\n有足够的船把我们庞大的军队运过去，是必不可少的。\n要是还能让海盗跟我们一起作战？那就更好了。

column5: Gryz made it clear that he wants to cut a deal.\nIn order to win them over, we'll need to bend to their will.\nHowever, after learning that, Alex and Nada have started to fight.
column6: 格瑞兹明确表示他想达成协议。\n为了拉拢他们，我们得顺着他们的意思来。\n然而，得知这一点后，亚历克斯和娜达开始争斗起来。

column5: Now we have to choose who we side with.\nThey both want different things, but they can both offer ships.\nThat's why we're here. I imagine they're waiting inside.
column6: 现在我们得选边站了。\n他们想要的东西各不相同，但都能提供船只。\n这就是我们来的原因。我想他们正在里面等着。

column5: He speaks with such passion and enthusiasm, it's enthralling.{w}\nIt was clear that he truly cared about Alestia and its people.
column6: 他说话时充满热忱和激情，令人着迷。{w}\n显然，他真心关心阿莱斯蒂亚和它的人民。

column5: The future of Mazeo is likely going to change. It's so exciting.\nI'll negotiate with them, and Gryz will make any necessary decrees.\nI just want my favorite people present, so that's why you're all here.
column6: 马泽奥的未来很可能会改变。真令人兴奋。\n我会跟他们谈判，格瑞兹会颁布必要的法令。\n我只想让我最喜欢的人在场，所以你们都来了。

column5: He smiles, and turns back to Ulric and Pro.
column6: 他笑了笑，转回身面向乌尔里克和普洛。

column5: I trust there aren't any objections?
column6: 我想应该没人反对吧？

column5: Ulric scoffs, crossing his arms.
column6: 乌尔里克哼了一声，抱起双臂。

column5: You sure upped the scale of our attack.\nI thought we just planned to steal a few ships.\nBut now you want an entire fleet? What changed?
column6: 你可把我们的行动规模拔高了不少。\n我还以为我们只打算偷几艘船。\n结果现在你想要整支舰队？什么变了？

column5: We need to give this our all if we're going to win.\nBut remember, we have a world to reshape when we're done.\nStriking a deal with the pirates is something that {i}needs{/i} to happen.
column6: 要想赢，我们就得全力以赴。\n但记住，事成之后我们还要重塑这个世界。\n跟海盗达成协议，是{i}必须{/i}要做的事。

column5: I mean, we {i}could{/i} wait until after the war.\nBut if we do it now, we stand a better chance of winning.\nPlus the people need to know that we're capable rulers, too.
column6: 我是说，我们{i}可以{/i}等战争结束后再说。\n但要是现在就做，我们获胜的机会更大。\n而且人们也需要知道，我们也是有能力统治的人。

column5: Fair enough. I concede.
column6: 有道理。我认输。

column5: Ulric smiles, the promise of more power and might appealing his curiosity.
column6: 乌尔里克笑了，更多权力与武力的许诺勾起了他的好奇。

column5: That's brilliant, Damek!\nTaking care of ten problems with one move — as usual.\nI'm just glad that they get to see for themselves, now.
column6: 太妙了，达梅克！\n一招解决十个问题——一如既往。\n我只是很高兴，他们现在能亲眼见识到了。

column5: He motions to Valessa, Fortaime and I.{w}\nThat seemed like a sound strategy, to be honest.{w}\nGain military might, {i}and{/i} prove himself capable of leadership.
column6: 他指了指瓦莱莎、福泰姆和我。{w}\n说实话，这似乎是稳妥的策略。{w}\n获取军力，{i}还{/i}证明了自己有领导才能。

column5: The people would need to know that he's worth following.{w}\nReleasing Mazeo from the grip of The Triumvirate woud be a great start.{w}\nAnd thankfully, Gryz was on our side. This wouldn't be possible otherwise.
column6: 人们需要知道他值得追随。{w}\n把马泽奥从三人执政团的掌控中解放出来，会是个绝佳的开端。{w}\n所幸格瑞兹站在我们这边。不然这根本不可能。

column5: Well, I guess it's time.\nI'm a little nervous, but I'll manage.
column6: 嗯，我想时候到了。\n我有点紧张，但我能应付。

column5: With a quick smirk, he's on his way inside.{w}\nPro and Ulric go too, expecting us to follow suit.
column6: 他匆匆一笑，动身走了进去。{w}\n普洛和乌尔里克也跟了进去，等着我们也跟上。

column5: Man, things are sure busy around here.\nI hope we get to rest when we get to our HQ.
column6: 天哪，这周围可真够忙的。\n希望到了总部能让我们歇歇。

column5: Come on Fortaime, it's interesting.\nWe're watching history in the making here.
column6: 别这样，福泰姆，这多有意思。\n我们正在见证历史的发生。

column5: If it's history, then it'll be in a book.\nI'd just sleep and read it when I get up.
column6: 要是它算历史，那总会写进书里。\n我干脆睡一觉，醒了再读就是了。

column5: They talk amongst themselves as they enter Gryz's house.{w}\nI guess I should hurry in, so I don't miss anything.
column6: 他们一边交谈一边走进格瑞兹的宅邸。{w}\n我想我该赶紧进去，免得错过什么。

column5: Signs point in every possible direction.{w}\nThey're labelled things like “Town Square” and “Residential District”.{w}\nA couple of the others say “Docks” and “Church of The Triumvirate.”
column6: 指示牌指向四面八方。{w}\n上面标着“城镇广场”和“住宅区”之类的字样。{w}\n还有几个写着“码头”和“三人执政团教堂”。

column5: I guess it was easy to find directions in Mazeo.{w}\nIt seems like The Rebel HQ is in the opposite direction.{w}\nAs I've learned, it's located in tunnels underneath the church.
column6: 看来在马泽奥辨认方向很容易。{w}\n反抗军总部似乎在反方向。{w}\n据我了解，它就位于教堂下方的隧道里。

column5: But stealing the tunnels underneath The Triumvirate's church?{w}\nSomething about that seems incredibly risky to me.{w}\nI'm sure Damek knows what he's doing, though.
column6: 可是偷用三人执政团教堂底下的隧道？{w}\n这在我看来风险大得离谱。{w}\n不过我相信达梅克清楚自己在做什么。

column5: Gryz's house is much more impressive than the others.{w}\nIt stands just as tall, but it's easily twice as wide.{w}\nHe must have tons of free space in there.
column6: 格瑞兹的宅邸比其他的气派得多。{w}\n高度相当，但宽度足足是别人的两倍。{w}\n里面想必有大把空地方。

column5: The residential district seems to go on forever.{w}\nBut it's all flat. There's no elevation like in Valinorth.{w}\nBack at home, social status was determined by how high you live.
column6: 住宅区似乎绵延无尽。{w}\n但这里一片平坦，不像瓦利诺斯那样有高低起伏。{w}\n在家乡，社会地位由你住得多高决定。

column5: The Elder lives right at the top, since he's the most important.{w}\nI was given a house right next to the Main Street, an easy walk to Mylus'.{w}\nI wonder how social status is determined in Mazeo. Maybe I'll ask Damek.
column6: 长老住在最顶端，因为他是最重要的人。{w}\n我分到的房子紧邻主街，走到迈勒斯家很方便。{w}\n不知道马泽奥的社会地位是怎么定的。也许我该问问达梅克。

column5: Gryz's house has a massive tree right next to it.{w}\nAt the very top, I can see some apples growing.{w}\nPerhaps those are the same ones Fortaime likes?
column6: 格瑞兹的宅邸旁边有棵巨大的树。{w}\n在最顶端，我能看到长出了一些苹果。{w}\n也许就是福泰姆爱吃的那些？

column5: Either way, they seem well maintained and fresh.{w}\nPerhaps this is Gryz's food of choice as well.
column6: 无论如何，它们看起来都照料得很好、很新鲜。{w}\n也许这也是格瑞兹钟爱的食物。

column5: When I enter Gryz's house, I'm taken aback by how massive it is.{w}\nA front desk, probably for his assistant, rests near the front door.{w}\nBut behind it is a massive atrium, with a staircase leading up.
column6: 我走进格瑞兹的宅邸时，被它的宏大吓了一跳。{w}\n前门附近有个前台，大概是给他助手用的。{w}\n但前台后面是个巨大的中庭，有楼梯通往楼上。

column5: I'm willing to bet that Gryz's office is at the top of that staircase.{w}\nI look around, and find Damek, Ulric and Pro chatting with a woman.{w}\nThis must be the assistant that Damek mentioned earlier.
column6: 我敢打赌格瑞兹的办公室就在楼梯顶端。{w}\n我环顾四周，发现达梅克、乌尔里克和普洛正在跟一个女人交谈。{w}\n这一定就是达梅克先前提到的那位助手。

column5: After noticing me enter, she quickly approaches us.{w}\nValessa and Fortaime retreat behind me, leaving me in charge.{w}\nI take a step forward and introduce myself to her without hesitation.
column6: 她注意到我进来后，快步走向我们。{w}\n瓦莱莎和福泰姆退到我身后，把场面交给我。{w}\n我上前一步，毫不犹豫地向她自我介绍。

column5: I've heard so much about you, [firstname].\nIt's a pleasure to finally meet you in person.
column6: 我听过太多关于你的事了，[firstname]。\n终于能亲自见到你，真高兴。

column5: I've heard so much about you, [firstname].\nIt's a pleasure to finally meet you in person.
column6: 我听过太多关于你的事了，[firstname]。\n终于能亲自见到你，真高兴。

column5: She puts her hand forward, and I give her a firm handshake.{w}\nValessa and Fortaime seem immediately at ease, as she's very friendly.{w}\nFor a moment, I'm not entirely sure what they were expecting.
column6: 她伸出手，我同她有力地握了握手。{w}\n因为她非常友善，瓦莱莎和福泰姆立刻放松下来。{w}\n有那么一瞬，我不太确定他们原本期待的是什么。

column5: I'm guessing that's The Blade of Exodus?
column6: 我猜那就是流亡之刃？

column5: She tilts her head toward my back.
column6: 她朝我背后偏了偏头。

column5: You can take that cloak off in here, by the way.\nEverybody in this office knows what's going on.\nThere's no need to hide around Gryz, or myself.
column6: 顺便说，你在这儿可以把斗篷脱掉。\n这间办公室里的人都知道是怎么回事。\n在格瑞兹和我面前，不必藏着掖着。

column5: I nod, and remove the makeshift hood covering my head.{w}\nI feel the fresh Mazean air on my face for the first time.
column6: 我点点头，摘下头上临时充当兜帽的东西。{w}\n我第一次感到马泽奥清新的空气拂过面庞。

column5: Come back here with the rest of us, alright?\nI think they're almost ready to head upstairs.
column6: 回来跟我们其他人待在一起吧，好吗？\n我想他们差不多准备好上楼了。

column5: She motions to the main landing area of the atrium.{w}\nWe move past her desk, which acts almost like a barrier.{w}\nI'm assuming she acts as Gryz's guard as well, standing watch.
column6: 她指了指中庭的主休息区。{w}\n我们走过她的桌子，那几乎像是一道屏障。{w}\n我猜她也兼任格瑞兹的守卫，负责放哨。

column5: After a few moments, we regroup with the others.{w}\nThey're talking amongst themselves, but Lillith brings that to an end.{w}\nClapping her hands together once, and very loudly, their attention is grabbed.
column6: 片刻之后，我们和其余人会合。{w}\n他们正彼此交谈，但莉莉丝终止了这一切。{w}\n她非常响亮地拍了一下手，吸引了他们的注意。

column5: Sorry, Lillith.\nJust lots to think about at the moment.\nI'm almost nervous to walk up there, if I'm honest.
column6: 抱歉，莉莉丝。\n眼下要操心的事太多了。\n老实说，我几乎有点不敢走上去。

column5: There's no need to be nervous, Damek.\nIt won't be any different from the last time you were here.\nJust a few added bodies, that's all. Not the end of the world.
column6: 没必要紧张，达梅克。\n这跟你上次来不会有什么不同。\n不过是多了几个人罢了。又不是天塌下来。

column5: I just don't want to make the wrong choice.\nThere's a lot riding on this, Lillith.
column6: 我只是不想做出错误的选择。\n这件事关系重大，莉莉丝。

column5: Have you made the wrong choice in the past...?
column6: 你过去做过错误的选择吗……？

column5: Well, I don't think so...
column6: 嗯，我想没有……

column5: Then you'll be fine.\nBesides, Alex and Nada aren't too bad.\nThey're both playing ball to get what they want.
column6: 那你就会没事的。\n再说，亚历克斯和娜达也没那么糟。\n他们俩都是为了得到想要的才肯配合。

column5: That means they'll have to be on their {i}best{/i} behavior.\nSo if being in the presence of pirates was a worry for—
column6: 这意味着他们必须表现得{i}最好{/i}。\n所以，要是与海盗共处一室让你担心——

column5: Oh no, that's not it at all.\nI'm more than happy to work with pirates.\nYou're right, though. I have a good track record.
column6: 哦不，完全不是那样。\n我非常乐意跟海盗合作。\n不过你说得对。我的过往记录一向不错。

column5: He lets out a nervous laugh before looking up to the top of the stairs.
column6: 他干笑一声，然后抬头望向楼梯顶端。

column5: I guess that'll have to do.\nAre they ready...?
column6: 我想这样也就够了。\n他们准备好了吗……？

column5: Yeah. They're expecting all of you.\nIt might be a bit crowded, but you'll manage.
column6: 嗯。他们在等你们所有人。\n可能会有点挤，但你们能应付。

column5: Did you happen to overhear anything?\nYou know, so I don't go in blind.
column6: 你有没有碰巧听到些什么？\n你知道的，免得我两眼一抹黑地进去。

column5: Unfortunately, no.\nThey're being {i}very{/i} discreet.
column6: 很遗憾，没有。\n他们{i}非常{/i}谨慎。

column5: Oh well, worth a shot.\nI guess it's finally time to do this.\nAre you ready everybody?
column6: 算了，试试也无妨。\n我想终于该做了。\n大家准备好了吗？

column5: He looks at all of us one by one, and we nod.{w}\nI can tell he's trying to delay this, but I'm not sure why.
column6: 他逐一看着我们每个人，我们纷纷点头。{w}\n我看得出他在设法拖延，但我不清楚为什么。

column5: Gryz will give me a debriefing when you're done.\nI know you're busy, so after this, just go on your way.\nLots to do, and little time to do it, right?
column6: 你们结束后，格瑞兹会向我做个简报。\n我知道你们忙，所以这之后就直接上路吧。\n要做的事很多，时间却很少，对吧？

column5: She glances at me, and the sword on my back before walking away.{w}\nIt seemed this quick detour wasn't going to be quick at all.{w}\nDuring these negotiations, everything could change.
column6: 她瞥了我一眼，又看了看我背上的剑，然后走开了。{w}\n看来这趟“顺路”根本快不了。{w}\n在这场谈判中，一切都可能改变。

column5: Hopefully, Damek would be able to get what he needs.{w}\nI just hope that the pirate's demands aren't too extreme.{w}\nWith the high ground, they had the right to request anything.
column6: 但愿达梅克能拿到他需要的东西。{w}\n我只希望海盗的条件别太离谱。{w}\n占据优势的他们，有权提出任何要求。

column5: We all look at the top of the stairs, ready to get things moving.{w}\nThis would be a very important moment for Damek and The Rebels.{w}\nTo that end, we shouldn't keep Gryz waiting for too much longer.
column6: 我们全都望向楼梯顶端，准备好让事情推进。{w}\n这对达梅克和反抗军来说，会是极其重要的时刻。{w}\n为此，我们不该让格瑞兹等太久。

column5: That's the door that leads to Gryz's office.{w}\nQuite the dramatic sight, if you ask me.{w}\nIt definitely makes him feel important.
column6: 那就是通往格瑞兹办公室的门。{w}\n要我说，这景象挺有戏剧性的。{w}\n这确实让他显得很有分量。

column5: Underneath the stairs, rests some sort of contraption.{w}\nIf I had to guess, it would be a statue representing a spirit idol.{w}\nThere's an artist's name and date on it. It must've been expensive.
column6: 楼梯下方放着某种装置。{w}\n要我猜，那是一座代表灵像的雕像。{w}\n上面刻着艺术家的名字和日期。一定价值不菲。

column5: Important papers are strewn about the desk.{w}\nIt's not my business to read them, but curiosity overtakes me.{w}\nI slowly approach the desk, and try my best to make out what I can.
column6: 重要的文件散落在桌上。{w}\n偷看不是我的事，但好奇心占据了我。{w}\n我慢慢走近桌子，尽力辨认能看清的内容。

column5: It seems to be a bunch of papers regarding upcoming shipments.{w}\nIt's correspondence between Gryz and the Mazeo Shipping Company.{w}\nUnderneath those papers is letters between Gryz and The Triumvirate.
column6: 似乎是一堆关于即将到来的货运的文件。{w}\n是格瑞兹与马泽奥航运公司之间的往来信件。{w}\n那些文件下面，是格瑞兹与三人执政团之间的信件。

column5: Hey, get away from there!\nThose papers aren't for your eyes.\nThat's top secret, only for The Mayor!
column6: 嘿，离那儿远点！\n那些文件不是给你看的。\n那是最高机密，只有市长才能看！

column5: Then why leave them out in the open like that...?{w}\nBefore I can continue, she gathers them up and takes them away.{w}\nShe's running all over the place. Lillith must be a busy girl.
column6: 那为什么把它们就那么摊在外面……？{w}\n我还没来得及多想，她就把它们收起来拿走了。{w}\n她到处跑来跑去。莉莉丝一定是个大忙人。

column5: Hey, Lillith...?
column6: 嘿，莉莉丝……？

column5: Yeah?
column6: 怎么了？

column5: Is there a library in Mazeo?\nLike, a place to read up on the spirits?\nI have some stuff I'd like to look into.
column6: 马泽奥有图书馆吗？\n就是，能查阅关于灵体的资料的地方？\n我有些东西想查一查。

column5: Unfortunately, no.\nThe Triumvirate seized all of that long ago.\nRumor has it that they've stuffed it all in Balteus.
column6: 很遗憾，没有。\n三人执政团很久以前就把那些都收缴了。\n有传言说，他们把那些全都塞进了巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: You mean at The Grand Library?
column6: 你是说在大图书馆？

column5: Yeah. But I don't know for sure.\nIt's just ancient rumors at this point.
column6: 对。但我也不确定。\n到现在这都只是古老的传言。

column5: Ancient...?
column6: 古老的……？

column5: There's a group of people that say so, yeah.\nThey think life existed on Alestia before The Triumvirate.\nWhen they took over, they just stole any writing saying otherwise.
column6: 确实有一群人这么说。\n他们认为在三人执政团之前，阿莱斯蒂亚上就有生命存在。\n他们掌权时，就把所有反过来说的文献都偷走了。

column5: That's impossible.
column6: 那不可能。

column5: Hey, I didn't say they were a {i}smart{/i} group.\nBut nobody has been to The Grand Library to see.\nThe Triumvirate keeps such a tight grip on Balteus.
column6: 嘿，我可没说他们是个{i}聪明{/i}的群体。\n但也没人去过那大图书馆一探究竟。\n三人执政团对巴尔泰乌斯的掌控太严密了。

column5: So they can't prove their theories...\nBut at the same time, we can't {i}disprove{/i} them.
column6: 所以他们无法证明自己的理论……\n但与此同时，我们也无法{i}反驳{/i}它们。

column5: Exactly.\nUnless you visit The Grand Libary.\nYou {i}are{/i} going to Balteus, right?
column6: 正是。\n除非你去那大图书馆看看。\n你们{i}确实{/i}要去巴尔泰乌斯，对吧？

column5: That's the end goal, yeah.
column6: 那是最终目标，没错。

column5: Then maybe we'll find out soon.\nWhatever knowledge they have in there? We deserve to know.\nI'm sure Damek will open its doors to everybody after the war.
column6: 那也许我们很快就能弄清楚了。\n不管那里面藏着什么知识？我们都有权知道。\n我相信战争结束后，达梅克会向所有人敞开它的大门。

column5: Who do you side with, Lillith?
column6: 你站在谁那边，莉莉丝？

column5: What do you mean?\nLike — between Alex and Nada?
column6: 你什么意思？\n是说——亚历克斯和娜达之间？

column5: Yeah, the pirates.\nI was just curious, that's all.
column6: 对，那些海盗。\n我只是好奇而已。

column5: Well, I don't know their demands.\nThat would play a big part in my choice.\nBut even then, it's not my place to decide.
column6: 嗯，我不知道他们的条件。\n那会对我的选择起很大作用。\n可即便如此，也轮不到我来决定。

column5: Oh, I'm not asking you to decide.\nIt's just a hypothetical question.
column6: 哦，我不是要你来决定。\n只是假设性地问问。

column5: Hmm...
Hey, take your time!\nIt's not an easy decision, after all.
column6: 嘿，慢慢想！\n毕竟这决定不容易做。

column5: Alex. Hands down.
column6: 亚历克斯。毫无疑问。

column5: Or you could answer instantly...\nBut why Alex? What makes him better?
column6: 或者你也可以秒答……\n但为什么是亚历克斯？他哪里更好？

column5: He treats me with respect, that's what.\nNada on the other hand, well that's a different story.\nThe way I look at things — there's two types of people.
column6: 他尊重我，就是这样。\n至于娜达，那就是另一回事了。\n在我看来——人有两种。

column5: Those that use others as stepping stones for success.\nAnd those that respect others, rising to the top together.\nNada is the former, and Alex is the latter. She's ruthless.
column6: 一种是把别人当作成功的垫脚石。\n另一种是尊重他人，一起爬上顶峰。\n娜达是前者，亚历克斯是后者。她心狠手辣。

column5: She's pretty much double-crossed everybody but Gryz.\nIf that ever happens, trust me, I won't be surprised at all.
column6: 除了格瑞兹，她几乎出卖过所有人。\n要是连他也被出卖，相信我，我一点都不会意外。

column5: How do we know we can trust her, then?
column6: 那我们怎么知道能相信她？

column5: Well, her and Alex have the edge in negotiations.\nThey have what {i}we{/i} want, so they can demand anything.\nI have no doubt that Nada will try to gain power and influence.
column6: 嗯，她和亚历克斯在谈判中占优势。\n他们手里有{i}我们{/i}想要的东西，所以能随意开价。\n我毫不怀疑娜达会试图攫取权力和影响力。

column5: These are the things she'd usually stab others in the back for.\nBut now she has an opportunity to get it just by {i}helping{/i} Gryz.
column6: 这些正是她往常会为此背后捅刀的东西。\n但现在她有机会仅靠{i}帮助{/i}格瑞兹就能得到。

column5: Oh, I guess that makes sense.\nShe's only in it to get what she wants.
column6: 哦，我想这说得通。\n她参与进来只是为了得到她想要的。

column5: Yeah. And Alex on the other hand...?\nI'm sure his demands will benefit more than him.\nThat's just the type of guy he is — so I like him more.
column6: 对。那亚历克斯呢……？\n我相信他的条件受益的不只是他自己。\n他就是那种人——所以我更喜欢他。

column5: Alright! Thanks for the information!
column6: 好！谢谢你的情报！

column5: No problem, little one.
column6: 不客气，小家伙。

column5: It's a book about the current state of piracy in Mazeo.
column6: 这是一本关于马泽奥海盗现状的书。

column5: There's a book sitting wide open on one of the desks.{w}\nIt seems to be a news article, and recently written, too.{w}\nI inspect it further, and learn that it details Mazeo's piracy.
column6: 有本书摊开在桌上。{w}\n似乎是一篇新闻报道，而且是最近写的。{w}\n我凑近细看，得知它详细讲述了马泽奥的海盗情况。

column5: I guess things are more complex than I thought.{w}\nIt's almost like Alex is fighting for more rights.{w}\nAll that divides the groups is one piece of paper?
column6: 我想事情比我以为的要复杂。{w}\n亚历克斯几乎像是在为更多权利而战。{w}\n把两派分开的，就只是一张纸？

column5: We all enter the office in sync, and everyone inside stares at us.{w}\nIt's odd, but, at first glance, I can tell exactly who everybody is.{w}\nNada takes a few steps forward, a sly smirk on her face.
column6: 我们一同走进办公室，里面所有人都盯着我们。{w}\n说来奇怪，可乍一看，我就能准确认出每个人是谁。{w}\n娜达上前几步，脸上挂着狡黠的坏笑。

column5: Late, are you?\nGood to know your word is trustworthy.\nIt's not like this is important, or anything like that.
column6: 迟到了，是吧？\n很高兴知道你的话还算可信。\n又不是说这件事有多重要，或者什么的。

column5: It's clear bait, and Damek doesn't take it at all.{w}\nInstead, he smirks back, and approaches Gryz and the pirates.
column6: 这明显是挑衅，而达梅克完全不接招。{w}\n他反而回以一笑，走向格瑞兹和那些海盗。

column5: Actually, this meeting doesn't start until {i}I{/i} arrive.\nSo, Nada, you're actually early. Very obedient of you.\nA bit softer than your reputation cites, but I'll let it slide.
column6: 其实，这场会议要等{i}我{/i}到了才开始。\n所以，娜达，你其实来早了。真是听话。\n比你传闻中要软一些，不过我不计较。

column5: She struggles to conjure up a comeback, and simply shrugs.{w}\nDamek approaches Gryz's desk, and waves us all over.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until we're all cramped together.
column6: 她憋了半天想找句话反击，最后只是耸了耸肩。{w}\n达梅克走向格瑞兹的桌子，招手让我们都过去。{w}\n没过多久，我们就全挤在了一起。

column5: Gryz, I'd like to introduce you to [firstname].
column6: 格瑞兹，我想向你介绍[firstname]。

column5: Gryz, I'd like to introduce you to [firstname].
column6: 格瑞兹，我想向你介绍[firstname]。

column5: I take a step forward, and offer a hand to Gryz.{w}\nHe rises from his chair, and gives my hand a firm shake.
column6: 我上前一步，向格瑞兹伸出手。{w}\n他从椅子上起身，有力地握了握我的手。

column5: It's an honor to meet you, [firstname].\nAnd those two must be your friends?
column6: 见到你是我的荣幸，[firstname]。\n那两位一定是你的朋友吧？

column5: It's an honor to meet you, [firstname].\nAnd those two must be your friends?
column6: 见到你是我的荣幸，[firstname]。\n那两位一定是你的朋友吧？

column5: I nod, as he looks at Valessa and Fortaime.
column6: 他看向瓦莱莎和福泰姆，我点了点头。

column5: Say, have you three been to Mazeo before?\nI can't put my finger on it, but you look familiar.
column6: 我说，你们三个以前来过马泽奥吗？\n我说不上来，但你们看着眼熟。

column5: I shake my head, and he promptly returns to his chair.{w}\nHe looks at all of us one-by-one, and lets out a loud sigh.
column6: 我摇摇头，他随即回到椅子上。{w}\n他逐一看着我们每个人，长叹一声。

column5: Oh well. Not that it matters, anyway.\nI'd like to thank you all for coming to my office.\nToday we discuss the matter of Damek and The Pirates.
column6: 算了。反正也不重要。\n感谢各位来到我的办公室。\n今天我们讨论达梅克与海盗的事。

column5: What have you got for me, Gryz?\nSurely you have their demands laid out on the table?
column6: 你有什么给我的，格瑞兹？\n他们的条件想必已经摆在桌上了吧？

column5: Yes, of course. I made them write up their demands in private.\nI didn't want them influencing each other in any certain direction.
column6: 是的，当然。我让他们私下各自写下条件。\n我不想让他们互相影响，往某个特定方向偏。

column5: He points to two pieces of paper resting on his table.{w}\nThey're turned upside down so nobody could read them.
column6: 他指向桌上放着的两张纸。{w}\n它们被扣着放，好让谁也读不到。

column5: Here's how this is going to work.\nNeither pirate knows which paper is theirs.\nDamek, you and your allies are to read each one.
column6: 接下来是这样进行的。\n两名海盗都不知道哪张纸是自己的。\n达梅克，你和你的盟友要分别阅读两份。

column5: Afterwards, each pirate is to explain their demands out loud.\nThis is to make sure they haven't gotten greedy, or changed their mind.\nWe also need some witnesses, which is why I had you bring some friends.
column6: 之后，每名海盗要当众说明自己的条件。\n这是为了确保他们没有贪心，或者改了主意。\n我们还需要一些见证人，所以我让你带几个朋友来。

column5: At that point, Damek may converse with his allies.\nWhen a decision is made, we will both sign the chosen demands.\nTo avoid conflict, neither pirate will learn if they were chosen.
column6: 到那时，达梅克可以与盟友商议。\n一旦做出决定，我们双方将在选中的条件上签字。\n为避免冲突，两名海盗都不会知道谁被选中了。

column5: When everybody leaves, the demands will be mailed back.\nThe pirate that receives a signed paper today, will know they were chosen.\nThere is no time for drama, or in-fighting on my property. Understand?
column6: 等所有人离开后，这些条件将被寄回。\n今天收到签字纸张的那名海盗，就会知道自己被选中了。\n在我的地盘上，没时间搞什么闹剧或内斗。明白吗？

column5: I understand.
column6: 我明白。

column5: Damek looks over to Nada and Alex, awaiting their approval.
column6: 达梅克看向娜达和亚历克斯，等待他们的认可。

column5: Yeah, I understand.
column6: 嗯，我明白。

column5: Me too.
column6: 我也是。

column5: Damek places his hands on the desk, looking over the papers.{w}\nBut before taking any actions, he turns his head toward me.
column6: 达梅克双手按在桌上，审视着那些文件。{w}\n但在采取任何行动之前，他转头看向我。

column5: [firstname], I'd like your input on this.\nYou're no stranger to tough decisions, right?
column6: [firstname]，我想听听你的意见。\n你对艰难的决定并不陌生，对吧？

column5: [firstname], I'd like your input on this.\nYou're no stranger to tough decisions, right?
column6: [firstname]，我想听听你的意见。\n你对艰难的决定并不陌生，对吧？

column5: And from what I've heard, we share some common views.\nIt couldn't hurt to get a second opinion from someone like you.
column6: 而且据我所闻，我们有些共同的看法。\n从你这样的人那里得到第二意见，总没坏处。

column5: I'd like to see how you think about this kind of stuff.\nYou must've had some reason to keep Peregrino, right?\nI'd like to see your \"process\", for lack of a better word.
column6: 我想看看你对这类事是怎么想的。\n你留下佩雷格里诺，一定有你的理由，对吧？\n我想看看你的“思路”，找不到更合适的说法。

column5: I nod, and walk up to the desk, standing beside him.{w}\nWe stare down at the two papers, hesitant.
column6: 我点点头，走到桌边，站在他身旁。{w}\n我们犹豫地低头盯着那两张纸。

column5: You may begin the first phase.\nRemain silent, but read the papers over.
column6: 你们可以开始第一阶段了。\n保持安静，读完这些文件。

column5: A few moments later, Damek grabs one of the papers.{w}\nHe inches closer to me, and slowly turns it around.
column6: 片刻之后，达梅克拿起其中一张纸。{w}\n他向我凑近，慢慢把它翻过来。

column5: It's Alex's offer.
column6: 是亚历克斯的条件。

column5: He wants the trade bans to be lifted from Mazeo.{w}\nIf this is done, the pirates must all be offered jobs in the Mazeo Shipping Company.{w}\nPiracy will be no more, and Mazeo will turn into a nation of \"free trade\".
column6: 他希望解除对马泽奥的贸易禁令。{w}\n若此事办成，所有海盗必须获得马泽奥航运公司的工作机会。{w}\n海盗将不复存在，马泽奥将变成一个“自由贸易”的国度。

column5: In exchange, he can offer the ships and crew of those who side with him.{w}\nThis makes up approximately 35 percent of the total pirates in Mazeo.{w}\nHe cannot guarantee how Nada's followers will react to this change.
column6: 作为交换，他能提供站在他这边那些人的船只和船员。{w}\n这约占马泽奥海盗总数的百分之三十五。{w}\n他无法保证娜达的追随者会对这一变动作何反应。

column5: Damek places the paper face down, and quickly grabs the other one.{w}\nHe shows no expression, wearing the perfect poker face.{w}\nTurning the paper around, it's time to see the other half.
column6: 达梅克把纸扣下，迅速拿起另一张。{w}\n他面无表情，摆出一副完美的扑克脸。{w}\n把纸翻过来，该看另一半了。

column5: It's Nada's offer.
column6: 是娜达的条件。

column5: She wants Mazeo to be divided into two.{w}\nIf this is done, all of the pirates will move to a new nation, out of Mazeo's way.{w}\nOf course, she must be declared head of this new pirate nation.
column6: 她希望马泽奥一分为二。{w}\n若此事办成，所有海盗都将迁往一个新国家，不再妨碍马泽奥。{w}\n当然，她必须被宣布为这个新海盗国家的首领。

column5: Furthermore, her demands include more details about the division of Mazeo.{w}\nIt's done so in a fashion that gives both sides equal market and residential space.{w}\nMazeo currently owns all of this, so it would negatively affect the nation.
column6: 此外，她的条件还包括关于马泽奥划分的更多细节。{w}\n其划分方式让双方获得同等的市场与居住空间。{w}\n这些目前都归马泽奥所有，因此会对这个国家造成不利影响。

column5: In exchange, she can offer approximately 65 percent of the total pirates in Mazeo.{w}\nThis includes a massive arsenal of ships, making Alex's offer seem inconsequential.{w}\nBoth demands share one thing in common: Pirates criminal records are to be wiped.
column6: 作为交换，她能提供马泽奥海盗总数约百分之六十五的力量。{w}\n其中包含庞大的舰船武备，让亚历克斯的条件显得微不足道。{w}\n两份条件有一个共同点：海盗的犯罪记录都将被抹去。

column5: Damek places the second paper face down, and shrugs.
column6: 达梅克把第二张纸扣下，耸了耸肩。

column5: Well I guess that's it, then?
column6: 那我想就这样了？

column5: Gryz nods.
column6: 格瑞兹点点头。

column5: Indeed, we can move on to phase two.\nAlex and Nada, it's your turn to step forward.\nYour verbal demands must match the papers.
column6: 确实，我们可以进入第二阶段了。\n亚历克斯、娜达，轮到你们上前了。\n你们口头陈述的条件必须与文件一致。

column5: In response to Gryz's order, they both step forward.{w}\nThis whole thing seemed incredibly well thought out.{w}\nThere was no room for error in any possible way.
column6: 听到格瑞兹的命令，两人都上前一步。{w}\n这整套流程考虑得极其周密。{w}\n任何环节都没有出错的余地。

column5: My demands are quite simple, actually.\nAll pirates will have their criminal records erased.\nFurthermore, the trade bans will be lifted from Mazeo.
column6: 我的条件其实很简单。\n所有海盗的犯罪记录都将被抹去。\n此外，对马泽奥的贸易禁令将被解除。

column5: Pirates will be publicly pardoned, and no longer ostracized.\nThey will be offered jobs within The Mazeo Shipping Company.\nOur clients, our cargo, and our trade routes will all carry over as well.
column6: 海盗将被公开赦免，不再遭受排斥。\n他们将获得马泽奥航运公司内的工作机会。\n我们的客户、货物和贸易航线也将一并延续。

column5: This will reintroduce us to society, and legitimize all of our efforts.\nMazeo will be free, as it once was, and as it always {i}should{/i} be.\nIn exchange, I offer 35 percent of Mazeo's pirates, and their ships.
column6: 这将让我们重新融入社会，让我们所有的努力变得名正言顺。\n马泽奥将重获自由，一如往昔，也一如它{i}本该{/i}的样子。\n作为交换，我献上马泽奥百分之三十五的海盗和他们的船只。

column5: He takes a few steps back, crossing his arms.{w}\nNada scoffs before vocalizing her demands.
column6: 他后退几步，抱起双臂。{w}\n娜达哼了一声，然后说出了她的条件。

column5: I can offer the other {i}65{/i} percent.\nI think that puts me a cut above Alex.
column6: 我能献上另外的{i}六十五{/i}个百分点。\n我想这让我比亚历克斯高出一筹。

column5: This certainly gets a reaction from others in the room.{w}\nHowever, we can't get won over by numbers.{w}\nWe were deciding the future of Mazeo.
column6: 这话果然让屋里其他人有了反应。{w}\n不过，我们不能被数字冲昏头脑。{w}\n我们决定的是马泽奥的未来。

column5: I also want all criminal records expunged.\nHowever, my other demands are a bit more extreme.\nI want Mazeo divided in half. I want a new nation born.
column6: 我也要求抹去所有犯罪记录。\n不过，我其他的条件要激进一些。\n我要马泽奥一分为二。我要一个新国家诞生。

column5: All pirates will move to this new nation, under {i}my{/i} lead.\nMazeo will no longer be able to interfere with our work.\nI will determine where the nation is split in half.
column6: 所有海盗都将迁往这个新国家，由{i}我{/i}来领导。\n马泽奥再也不能干涉我们的营生。\n国家从何处一分为二，由我来定。

column5: I want both residential {i}and{/i} commercial land.\nWe will be given everything we need to live happily.\nThat is my demand. A new nation, built for piracy.
column6: 我要住宅用地，{i}也要{/i}商业用地。\n我们要得到幸福生活所需的一切。\n这就是我的条件。一个为海盗而建的新国家。

column5: She steps back, content with what she said.{w}\nGryz turns to face Damek and myself again.
column6: 她后退一步，对自己的话很满意。{w}\n格瑞兹再次转身面向达梅克和我。

column5: Does that align with the demands on paper?
column6: 这与纸上的条件一致吗？

column5: Yes, I believe it does.\nWhat was the next step again?
column6: 是的，我想是一致的。\n下一步是什么来着？

column5: You may take some time to think.\nTalk with your allies, and then give me an answer.
column6: 你们可以花点时间考虑。\n跟你的盟友商议，然后给我答复。

column5: Oh, right. Sorry, my mind is all over the place.\nThere's no need to think, I already have my answer.
column6: 哦，对。抱歉，我脑子里一团乱。\n不需要再考虑了，我已经有答案了。

column5: Oh, is that so...?
column6: 哦，是吗……？

column5: Yeah, of course.\nThis one was simple for me.
column6: 对，当然。\n这个选择对我来说很简单。

column5: He crosses his arms, and turns to face me.
column6: 他抱起双臂，转身面向我。

column5: What about you...?\nWho would you choose?
column6: 你呢……？\n你会选谁？

column5: I point to the paper that contained Alex's demands.{w}\nDamek laughs and then gives me a wide smile.
column6: 我指向那张写有亚历克斯条件的纸。{w}\n达梅克笑了，然后朝我咧嘴一笑。

column5: I point to the paper that contained Nada's demands.{w}\nDamek laughs and then gives me a wide smile.
column6: 我指向那张写有娜达条件的纸。{w}\n达梅克笑了，然后朝我咧嘴一笑。

column5: Great minds think alike, I suppose.\nGood to know we had the same idea.\nLet's sign this one, Gryz. It's my final choice.
column6: 我想英雄所见略同。\n很高兴知道我们想法一致。\n我们签这一份吧，格瑞兹。这是我最终的选择。

column5: He points to the same paper, and Gryz brings out a quill.{w}\nThey waste no time in signing it, making it an official decree.{w}\nAfter that, Gryz rolls both papers up, and seals them with wax.
column6: 他指向同一张纸，格瑞兹取出一支羽毛笔。{w}\n他们毫不耽搁地签了字，使其成为正式法令。{w}\n之后，格瑞兹把两份纸都卷起来，用蜡封好。

column5: Nada, Alex, thank you both for your kind offers.\nI'll have these mailed back to you right away.\nYou'll know within a few hours, I'm sure.
column6: 娜达、亚历克斯，感谢你们两位的慷慨条件。\n我会立刻把这两份寄回给你们。\n我相信，几小时内你们就会知道结果。

column5: Sounds good to me.
column6: 我没意见。

column5: This one's as good as mine.
column6: 这一份就跟到手了一样。

column5: After saying their final words, they both leave.{w}\nAn awkward silence overtakes the room.
column6: 说完最后的话，两人都离开了。{w}\n一阵尴尬的沉默笼罩了房间。

column5: You're all free to talk again, you know.\nWe just didn't want Alex and Nada to know Damek's choice.
column6: 你们现在可以随便说话了。\n我们只是不想让亚历克斯和娜达知道达梅克的选择。

column5: After hearing that, everybody is at ease.{w}\nTalking amongst themselves, they theorize who we chose.
column6: 听到这话，大家都放松下来。{w}\n他们彼此交谈，猜测我们选了谁。

column5: Well, Damek?
column6: 那么，达梅克？

column5: Who did you choose!?
column6: 你选了谁！？

column5: Oh, you'll find out soon enough.\nSorry for this little detour, everybody.\nWe can make our way back to HQ now.
column6: 哦，你们很快就会知道了。\n各位，抱歉绕了这么一小段路。\n我们现在可以回总部了。

column5: Though I think we should cut through the docks.\nIt's crowded, but it'll make for a nice shortcut.\nWe're already running behind schedule.
column6: 不过我想我们该从码头穿过去。\n那儿人多，但是条不错的近路。\n我们进度已经落后了。

column5: He sneers at Pro, who quickly backs off.{w}\nUlric takes the message as well, and stops asking.
column6: 他朝普洛冷笑一下，普洛立刻缩了回去。{w}\n乌尔里克也领会了意思，不再追问。

column5: I hope you got what you needed, Damek.\nAttacking Balteus will be no easy feat.
column6: 希望你得偿所愿，达梅克。\n进攻巴尔泰乌斯绝非易事。

column5: We'll be more than fine, Gryz.\nI trust you can handle things from here?
column6: 我们会没事的，格瑞兹。\n我相信这里的事你能处理好？

column5: Of course. But there may be some contempt coming.\nDon't be surprised if Alex or Nada comes fuming to you.
column6: 当然。但可能会招来一些怨恨。\n要是亚历克斯或娜达怒气冲冲地来找你，别意外。

column5: Of course.\nThank you so much, Gryz.\nWe couldn't do this without you.
column6: 当然。\n太感谢你了，格瑞兹。\n没有你我们办不成这事。

column5: Don't worry about it.\nJust make sure I don't regret this.\nCrossing The Triumvirate is a {i}bad{/i} idea.
column6: 别客气。\n只要确保我不会后悔就行。\n跟三人执政团作对可不是{i}好{/i}主意。

column5: You won't, I promise.\nIf you'll excuse us though, we need to go.\nI still have to give them the grand tour, after all.
column6: 你不会的，我保证。\n不过失陪了，我们得走了。\n毕竟我还得带他们好好参观一番。

column5: Gryz nods, and it seems we're dismissed.{w}\nI guess our next step was to head to the docks.{w}\nDamek sure seems excited about this tour.{w}
column6: 格瑞兹点点头，看来我们可以告退了。{w}\n我想我们的下一步是前往码头。{w}\n达梅克对这趟参观显然很兴奋。{w}

column5: Alright, let's go.\nI'll make the announcement back at HQ.\nWe have a new ally, and a lot more power.
column6: 好了，我们走。\n我会回总部宣布消息。\n我们有了新盟友，还有了强大得多的力量。

column5: He holds a closed fist up to his chest, resolute.
column6: 他把握紧的拳头抵在胸前，神情坚定。

column5: We're going to do this. I know it.
column6: 我们一定能做成。我知道。

column5: And with that, it's time to get things on the move.{w}\nI'd finally start training, and see The Rebellion's new HQ.
column6: 就这样，该动身了。{w}\n我终于要开始训练，并一睹反抗军的新总部。

column5: Gryz's desk reminds me of Mylus' place.{w}\nIt's messy, but he still has it under control.{w}\nEverything is where it needs to be, and it works.
column6: 格瑞兹的桌子让我想起迈勒斯那儿。{w}\n乱是乱，但他仍然掌控得住。{w}\n每样东西都在该在的位置，运转良好。

column5: There's a ton of papers on the floor.{w}\nI inspect them closer. They're all dated for today.{w}\nCould Gryz's job really be {i}that{/i} busy!? Wow.
column6: 地上堆着海量的文件。{w}\n我凑近查看，日期全是今天。{w}\n格瑞兹的工作真有{i}那么{/i}忙吗！？哇。

column5: I look over at Fortaime, and he's shaking.{w}\nI can tell the mess is bothering him.{w}\nBut he also knows he can't touch it.
column6: 我看向福泰姆，他在发抖。{w}\n我看得出这片凌乱让他难受。{w}\n但他也知道自己不能碰。

column5: Gryz's office seems to overlook the Mazean Docks.{w}\nA massive shipyard, full of impressive vessels.{w}\nI see people loading them up, preparing shipments.
column6: 格瑞兹的办公室似乎俯瞰着马泽奥码头。{w}\n一个巨大的造船厂，停满令人印象深刻的船只。{w}\n我看到人们正在往船上装货，准备发运。

column5: I wonder how he could work next to such a loud place.{w}\nIt shows no signs of slowing down, and it's very busy.{w}\nWe'd be heading there next, and I couldn't wait.
column6: 我纳闷他怎么能在这般喧闹的地方工作。{w}\n那里毫无放慢的迹象，忙得不可开交。{w}\n我们接下来就要去那儿，我迫不及待。

column5: I start to inspect the bookshelf, but Gryz quickly stops me.
column6: 我正要查看书架，格瑞兹立刻制止了我。

column5: Hey, don't touch any of that.\nThis is my office, you know.
column6: 嘿，别碰那些东西。\n你知道，这是我的办公室。

column5: He crosses his arms, and I back away from the shelf.{w}\nSomething tells me I wouldn't want to get on his bad side.
column6: 他抱起双臂，我从书架旁退开。{w}\n我有种感觉，我可不想惹上他。

column5: It's a map of Alestia.{w}\nI see everything on here:{w}\nValinorth, Mazeo, Alarinthia, and Balteus.
column6: 这是一张阿莱斯蒂亚的地图。{w}\n上面的一切我都看得到：{w}\n瓦利诺斯、马泽奥、阿拉林西亚，还有巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: Only the west remains unmapped.{w}\nVicious storms and unruly waters get in the way.{w}\nIt's unlikely that anything is out there, though.
column6: 只有西部仍是未标注之地。{w}\n凶猛的暴风雨和狂暴的海域横亘其间。{w}\n不过，那外面不太可能有什么东西。

column5: Hey, Gryz?
column6: 嘿，格瑞兹？

column5: Yes?
column6: 什么事？

column5: What's with that sheep around your neck?
column6: 你脖子上那只羊是怎么回事？

column5: Oh, you mean Lassiter?
column6: 哦，你说的是拉西特？

column5: I guess...?
column6: 大概吧……？

column5: When I was younger, I used to be a shepherd.\nBut that didn't last long before I served The Triumvirate.\nThey made me kill all my sheep before they accepted me.
column6: 我年轻时当过牧羊人。\n但没过多久，我就去为三人执政团效力了。\n他们逼我杀光了我所有的羊，才肯接纳我。

column5: What!?
column6: 什么！？

column5: I guess it was to prove myself.\nYou know, that I'd leave my old life behind.\nI did what they said, but I kept a souvenir.
column6: 我猜是为了证明我自己。\n你知道，证明我会抛下过去的生活。\n我照他们说的做了，但我留下了一件纪念品。

column5: Oh, I see...
column6: 哦，我明白了……

column5: It's always important to remember where you came from.\nDid you bring any souvenirs from Valinorth along with you?
column6: 记住自己从何而来，永远很重要。\n你从瓦利诺斯带什么纪念品来了吗？

column5: Actually, no...\nUnless my clothes count.
column6: 其实，没有……\n除非我的衣服算得上。

column5: Depends who you're asking.
column6: 那得看问的是谁。

column5: But you know, I'm not actually leaving Valinorth behind!\nWe'll save it, and go back one day. I know it...\nThat's one of our goals during this journey.
column6: 但你知道，我其实并没有抛下瓦利诺斯！\n我们会救下它，总有一天会回去。我知道……\n这是我们这趟旅程的目标之一。

column5: I see...
column6: 我明白了……

column5: You let Gryz have his redemption.
column6: 你让格瑞兹得到了他的救赎。

column5: You tapped into the power of the Spirit Idol yourself.
column6: 你亲自汲取了灵像的力量。

column5: You used the spiritual energy to create Monarch Vessels.
column6: 你利用灵性能量创造了君主容器。

column5: You used the spiritual energy to create Artificial Seers.
column6: 你利用灵性能量创造了人造先知。

column5: You appointed Howl as the Monarch Advisor.
column6: 你任命豪尔为君主顾问。

column5: You appointed Damek as the Monarch Advisor.
column6: 你任命达梅克为君主顾问。

column5: After we enter the door, we spend a few minutes descending into darkness.{w}\nSoon enough, however, we reach an area with torches lighting the way.{w}\nIt seems to mark a path straight forward. This must be it.
column6: 我们进门之后，花了几分钟向下走入黑暗。{w}\n不过很快，我们来到一处有火把照亮的地方。{w}\n火把似乎标出了一条笔直向前的路。就是这里了。

column5: Wow, it's so dark!\nI can't even see where I'm going.
column6: 哇，好黑啊！\n我连自己要往哪儿走都看不见。

column5: Just give it a few minutes. Your eyes will adjust.\nI remember my first time down here. I was terrified.
column6: 等几分钟就好。你的眼睛会适应的。\n我还记得第一次来这儿，我吓坏了。

column5: He presses his back against the wall and waits.{w}\nWe all do the same, and wait around until we can see.
column6: 他背靠着墙，等待着。{w}\n我们都照做，原地等着直到能看清东西。

column5: The torches only help so much.\nWe put a majority of them in our actual HQ.\nBasically, we only have them down here to—
column6: 火把能帮的有限。\n我们把大部分火把都放在真正的总部了。\n基本上，我们把它们放在这儿只是为了——

column5: He cuts himself off and looks further down the tunnel.
column6: 他打住话头，望向隧道更深处。

column5: Everyone, quiet.\nBacks against the wall. Now.
column6: 所有人，安静。\n背靠墙。快。

column5: We do as instructed, and I notice an aura of fear overtake us.{w}\nI stare down the tunnels, and I see a suit of armor start to emerge.{w}\nWhite and gold, just like my vision. It takes slow, clunky steps.
column6: 我们照做，我注意到一股恐惧的气息笼罩了我们。{w}\n我盯着隧道深处，看见一副铠甲开始浮现。{w}\n白色与金色，正如我幻象中所见。它迈着缓慢笨重的步子。
